answer: Like a willow, an identity bond should bend but not break: require every agent to lock collateral that vests slowly over weeks, so a Sybil farmer faces a spiral of rising cost, with each new identity demanding fresh locked capital plus a waiting period before it can earn. Honest agents meanwhile build a reef of mutual attestation history no newcomer can fake overnight. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a thousand rooted, attested ones costs more than any reward they could extract.
